wars.name: Chu-Zeng wars

zones.text: Zeng, 'territory in the area around Suizhou in modern Hubei province' (findings 'reached up to the south west border of Henan province')

wars.outcome: King Wu of Chu invaded Zeng in 706 and attacked again in 704 (Zeng lost the Battle of Suqi, peace followed that year); Wu died on an expedition into Zeng in 690; in 640 the vassals led by Zeng attacked Chu and were beaten; after Chengpu (632) 'Zeng was reduced to the status of Chu vassal, no longer independent'. No border change is dated.
wars.note: Du Yu believed Chu later 'restored Zeng's independence as a marquessate'. In 506, when Wu took Ying, King Zhao of Chu fled to Zeng, which refused Wu's demand and was rewarded by Chu. The vassalage after 632 is the chu dossier's to carry (vassal_start, counterpart zeng); it is not written here because the schema puts the event in the suzerain's ledger.

certainty.note: No Zeng boundary is on the page; soft throughout.

notes: Pages opened (2 of 1-2): Zeng (state), Chu (state). Wikidata id left null (unreachable). Sui (隨) and Zeng (曾) are one place on the best-supported view in the Zeng page (Li Xueqin: 'the states of Sui and Zeng were actually the same place'; Ren Wei: 'Zeng conquered and occupied the state of Sui'); the 'Sui (state)' article redirects to a Zeng-titled page. This dossier is Zeng-Sui; the chu dossier's 480 bridge 'Dao, Ruo, Zhongli, Sui and other states' covers the same land. START -1045 is the first year of the Western Zhou span the page gives, a bridge (confidence 1). END -401 is the last year of 'the 5th century BC', a bound, also confidence 1: no page gives the year. Marquis Yi of Zeng (the bianzhong tomb) is on a separate page not opened; the Chu page only says the Chu king 'attended the Marquis's funeral at Suizhou'. SUIZHOU is not a gazetteer place (coordinates used). AREA: none on the page. The Chu dossier needs a vassal_start for Zeng after 632 and a gain at the end.
